newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian stocks close firm, outlook cloudy.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian stocks close firm, outlook cloudy.

text.p: Slovenian shares closed firmer on Tuesday in what traders said was a technical reaction to recent losses, but market participants said political uncertainty continued to cloud the bourse's short-term outlook.
"Everoyone is waiting for something that could move the market," said Miha Dolinar, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska banka.

The 10-share SBI index rose 0.65 percent or 7.45 points to close at 1,167.2. The index has lost some 4.7 percent since a general election on November 10 resulted in a stand-off between leftist and centre-right parties.
Traders said activity on the market was likely to remain muted until fresh clues on the formation of the country's next government emerge.
Turnover rose to 78.9 million tolars from 66.8 million. Overall 12 shares rose and six fell, while seven were untraded.
Drug producer Lek's issue A was the most actively traded share, rising 0.80 percent or 150 tolars to 19,000 tolars on volume of 1,754 shares.

The stock made its debut on the Ljubljana bourse in September and has attracted significant interest particularly from international investors, boosting trading volumes and helping the market to recover from a prolonged summer lull.
Bank UBK was the day's biggest gainer, firming 10 percent to 6,820 tolars on volume of only two shares.
Brokerage Nika was the leading decliner, falling 5.66 percent to 3,950 tolars on volume of 1,221 shares.
